label: Governor
term_limit: No more than 8 years in any 12-year period
what_it_does: Chief executive of the state. Signs or vetoes bills, appoints agency heads and judges to fill vacancies where the law allows, and proposes the state budget.

label: Lieutenant Governor
what_it_does: Presides over the Senate and succeeds the Governor if the office becomes vacant.

label: Attorney General
what_it_does: The state's lawyer. Represents the state in court.

label: Secretary of State
what_it_does: Oversees the state elections division and business filings.

label: Treasurer of State
what_it_does: Manages the state's cash and investments.

label: State Comptroller (formerly Auditor of State)
what_it_does: Keeps the state's books: pays state employees, distributes tax dollars and prepares year-end financial reports. Audits of state and local governments are done by the State Board of Accounts.

label: State Senator
vacancy_rule: Caucus of the departing member's party precinct committeepersons in the district (IC 3-13-5)
what_it_does: One of 50 members of the Senate. Terms are staggered so about half the seats are on the ballot every two years.

label: State Representative
vacancy_rule: Caucus of the departing member's party precinct committeepersons in the district (IC 3-13-5)
what_it_does: One of 100 members of the House. All seats are on the ballot every two years.

label: County commissioner
vacancy_rule: Party caucus, where a statute calls for one (IC 3-13-11)
what_it_does: A member of the board of commissioners, the county's executive body. Handles county property, roads and bridges, contracts and appointments to boards. Some counties differ by statute, including how commissioners are elected (by district or countywide).

label: County council member
vacancy_rule: Party caucus, where a statute calls for one (IC 3-13-11)
what_it_does: A member of the county's fiscal body. Approves the annual budget, sets salaries and tax rates, and approves borrowing. Seat structure varies by statute: most counties use 4 district and 3 at-large seats; counties of 185,000 to 300,000 people that opted in by September 1, 2023 use nine single-member districts.

label: County auditor
term_limit: 8 years in any 12 (Ind. Const. Art. 6 sec. 2)
vacancy_rule: Party caucus, where a statute calls for one (IC 3-13-11)
what_it_does: Keeps county financial records, prepares tax bills and certifies the budget.

label: Clerk of the Circuit Court
term_limit: 8 years in any 12 (Ind. Const. Art. 6 sec. 2)
vacancy_rule: Party caucus, where a statute calls for one (IC 3-13-11)
what_it_does: Keeps court records and, in many counties, helps run elections.

label: County recorder
term_limit: 8 years in any 12 (Ind. Const. Art. 6 sec. 2)
vacancy_rule: Party caucus, where a statute calls for one (IC 3-13-11)
what_it_does: Keeps official records of land transactions such as deeds and mortgages.

label: County treasurer
term_limit: 8 years in any 12 (Ind. Const. Art. 6 sec. 2)
vacancy_rule: Party caucus, where a statute calls for one (IC 3-13-11)
what_it_does: Collects property taxes and distributes them to local units.

label: Sheriff
term_limit: 8 years in any 12 (Ind. Const. Art. 6 sec. 2)
vacancy_rule: Party caucus, where a statute calls for one (IC 3-13-11)
what_it_does: Runs the county jail, serves court papers and provides law enforcement in the county.

label: Coroner
term_limit: 8 years in any 12 (Ind. Const. Art. 6 sec. 2)
vacancy_rule: Party caucus, where a statute calls for one (IC 3-13-11)
what_it_does: Investigates deaths that are sudden, unexplained or suspicious and determines cause and manner of death.

label: County surveyor
term_limit: None (a constitutional office, but not on the 8-in-12 list)
vacancy_rule: Party caucus, where a statute calls for one (IC 3-13-11)
what_it_does: Keeps county survey records and oversees drainage and legal drains.

label: County assessor
vacancy_rule: Party caucus, where a statute calls for one (IC 3-13-11)
what_it_does: Determines the assessed value of property in the county for tax purposes.

label: Prosecuting attorney
term_limit: None (a judicial officer; not on the 8-in-12 list)
what_it_does: Brings criminal charges in county courts on behalf of the state.

label: Circuit court judge
what_it_does: Presides over the county's circuit court. Judges of circuit courts are elected in partisan races in most counties.

label: Superior court judge (merit selection counties)
vacancy_rule: A local judicial nominating commission sends the Governor the five most highly qualified nominees and the Governor appoints. If voters reject a judge, the Governor fills the vacancy.
what_it_does: In four counties (Lake, St. Joseph, Allen and Marion) superior court judges are chosen by merit selection, not partisan election. Each judge serves a 6-year term and then faces a yes-or-no retention vote at the general election before the term ends.

label: Township trustee
vacancy_rule: Party caucus, where a statute calls for one (IC 3-13-11)
what_it_does: The township executive. Must live in the township; the term starts January 1 after the election. Provides township services such as poor relief and often fire protection.

label: Township board member
vacancy_rule: Party caucus, where a statute calls for one (IC 3-13-11)
what_it_does: One of three members of the township board, which approves the township budget and tax rate. At-large partisan seats; straight-party voting applies to at-large seats from 2027.

label: Mayor
vacancy_rule: Party caucus, where a statute calls for one (IC 3-13-11)
what_it_does: The city's executive. Runs city departments, proposes the budget and can veto council ordinances.

label: City council member
vacancy_rule: Party caucus, where a statute calls for one (IC 3-13-11)
what_it_does: A member of the city's legislative body. Passes ordinances and approves the city budget. In second-class cities the council has district and at-large seats; straight-party voting applies to at-large seats from 2027.

label: City clerk
vacancy_rule: Party caucus, where a statute calls for one (IC 3-13-11)
what_it_does: Keeps city records and council minutes. Elected in second-class cities.

label: Town council member
vacancy_rule: Party caucus, where a statute calls for one (IC 3-13-11)
what_it_does: A member of the town's governing body. Passes ordinances and approves the town budget.

label: Town clerk-treasurer
vacancy_rule: Party caucus, where a statute calls for one (IC 3-13-11)
what_it_does: Keeps town records and handles town money in towns where the office is elected.

label: School board member
vacancy_rule: Party caucus for school board seats where IC 20-23-4-30 calls for one (IC 3-13-11)
what_it_does: Sets school policy, adopts the school budget and hires the superintendent. Since SEA 287 (2025) a candidate may list a party, list independent, or list no party; there is no primary. Some boards have appointed seats.

label: Library board trustee
term_limit: Up to 4 consecutive terms (per State Library blog; not re-read)
what_it_does: Appointed member of a public library board that sets library policy and budget.

label: Precinct committeeperson
what_it_does: Elected in the primary as a local party officer. Precinct committeepersons take part in caucuses that fill many legislative and local vacancies.

label: Probate court judge
vacancy_rule: (not sourced)
what_it_does: Presides over the St. Joseph Probate Court, which state law sets up as a separate court for St. Joseph County. The judge is elected by the county's voters at the general election for a six-year term.

label: Township assessor
vacancy_rule: Party caucus, where a statute calls for one (IC 3-13-11)
what_it_does: Carries out property assessment in the township. Elected only in townships that had at least 15,000 parcels of real property on January 1, 2008 and whose voters rejected moving assessment to the county assessor in a referendum. Elsewhere the county assessor does this work. Four-year term.

label: Town court judge
vacancy_rule: (not sourced)
what_it_does: Presides over a town court. A town may set up or abolish its court by ordinance, but only in the years the law allows (2026, then every fourth year). The judge is elected by the town's voters, normally for four years.
